what_it_is: The exact three-dimensional shape of a made thing, as solids and surfaces
examples: B-rep solid, CAD part or assembly, feature tree, NURBS surfaces, sheet-metal model, hull form, implicit or lattice model

what_it_is: A shape or a region cut into elements or points for computing on
examples: finite element mesh, CFD grid, voxels, point cloud, triangulated surface, STL

what_it_is: A two-dimensional technical drawing or sketch of a made thing
examples: dimensioned drawing, sketch, flat pattern, section, detail drawing, plan sheet

what_it_is: The design of a building, structure or piece of land
examples: building information model, floor plan, structural frame, road alignment, grading surface, piping or duct layout, site plan

what_it_is: The design of a circuit or chip
examples: schematic, netlist, PCB layout, IC layout, HDL, footprint, stackup

what_it_is: An engineered or natural system described as connected parts and equations, ready to simulate or analyse
examples: power grid model, pipe network, process flowsheet, control block diagram, multibody model, reservoir model, plant model

what_it_is: Instructions a machine runs to make or move something
examples: toolpath, G-code, robot program, PLC logic, print slices, nesting layout, inspection program

what_it_is: How something is to be made or done, step by step
examples: routing, work instructions, recipe, operation sequence, setup sheet, procedure, protocol, test plan

what_it_is: What a product or system is made of, as a list or tree of items
examples: bill of materials, part list, item master, product configuration, catalog of components

what_it_is: What a material is and how it behaves
examples: material properties, alloy composition, stress-strain curve, constitutive model, fluid properties

what_it_is: What a design or system is subjected to in an analysis
examples: loads, boundary conditions, operating conditions, load cases, excitation, duty cycle

what_it_is: Computed physical behaviour of a design or system
examples: stress, deflection, temperature or flow fields, natural frequencies, safety margins, energy use, predicted yield, performance curves

what_it_is: What a design, product or service must satisfy
examples: requirements, specifications, design criteria, tolerances, standards to meet, acceptance criteria, engineering constraints

what_it_is: What instruments or tests recorded about a real thing
examples: sensor signals, telemetry, waveforms, lab results, inspection measurements, test data, vital signs, meter readings

what_it_is: A still picture of something real
examples: photograph, scan, radiograph, micrograph, satellite or aerial image, video frame

what_it_is: Recorded sound or moving pictures
examples: speech, music, call recording, video footage

what_it_is: Where things are on the earth
examples: map layers, terrain or elevation, parcels, addresses, coordinates, road or utility networks as geography, boundaries

what_it_is: Observed or given conditions of the natural world
examples: weather, climate, soil, geology, hydrology, ocean or air quality observations

what_it_is: The structure of a molecule or a biological sequence
examples: chemical structure, protein structure, genome sequence, compound library, crystal structure

what_it_is: Prose written to be read by people
examples: report written by a person, contract, letter, article, manual, email, notes, transcript, filing, completed form, lesson content

what_it_is: A creative work or its layout, made to be seen or heard
examples: graphic, page layout, animation, 3D scene for film or games, typography, user interface mock-up, edited video timeline

what_it_is: Instructions a computer runs, and what configures them
examples: source code, script, query, configuration, binary, container image, infrastructure definition, schema

what_it_is: A model fitted or trained on data, and the data prepared for it
examples: trained model, fitted parameters, labelled training set, embeddings

what_it_is: A maintained collection that many tasks look things up in
examples: code sets, drug database, tool library, component library, templates, ontology, standards database, rate tables published by others

what_it_is: What is held about an individual
examples: patient record, customer or contact record, employee file, student record, applicant, member account, identity

what_it_is: A recorded exchange or commitment between parties
examples: order, invoice, payment, claim, booking, shipment, ledger entry, receipt, trade

what_it_is: What is owned and owed, summed up
examples: balances, financial statements, portfolio holdings, valuation, tax return, account totals

what_it_is: What something costs or is charged at
examples: prices, costs, quotes, estimates, budgets, rates, tariffs, fees

what_it_is: What is on hand and what can be used
examples: stock levels, asset register, equipment list, fleet, capacity, resource availability, bed or seat availability

what_it_is: What happens when
examples: schedule, timetable, calendar, roster, appointments, production sequence in time

what_it_is: A path through space
examples: route, path, trajectory, flight plan, tour, toolless motion path of a vehicle

what_it_is: What has been decided or is recommended to be done
examples: plan, allocation, assignment, recommendation, dispatch, treatment plan, strategy, approval or denial

what_it_is: A statement about a future quantity
examples: demand forecast, weather forecast, projection, predicted failure date, expected revenue

what_it_is: A judgment of one thing as a number or a label
examples: score, ranking, risk rating, grade, diagnosis code, category label, match or no match

what_it_is: What state something is in or what just happened to it
examples: status, state, event stream, alert, alarm, notification, incident, log of actions, audit trail

what_it_is: Figures computed from data and set out for someone to read
examples: statistics, KPIs, dashboard, chart, compliance report, variance report, audit findings, summary tables

what_it_is: What is permitted, required or owed, set by an authority or by management
examples: law, regulation, policy, business rules, eligibility rules, contract terms as rules, tax rules, pay rules, approval rules

what_it_is: Who may do what
examples: credentials, permissions, roles, keys, certificates, licences

what_it_is: Records in rows and fields that fit no kind above. Use only when nothing more specific fits
examples: generic database table, list of items, record set, history of values, dataset

what_it_is: A number or a choice someone gives for this one run. Not made by another tool
examples: tolerance for an operation, time window, threshold, option, target value, number of iterations, type of analysis, step size

what_it_is: Not information: a thing or a person present
examples: specimen, sample, part on the machine, raw material, the patient in the room

what_it_is: None of the above fits. Say in the note what it is
